# Hands Take Stage — local browser interface
No AI backend, account, persistent storage, uploads, external art, fonts, or audio assets.
Wait for window.puppetStage before calling the API.

URLs:
/ : real WebXR hands, tabletop stage a, six-step introduction.
/?emu=1&panel=1&stage=placeholder : IWER hands and touch-friendly emulation panel.
?stage=a : default tabletop theatre. ?stage=placeholder retains the original. Unknown names in URLs fall back to a.
?fps=1 : optional board fps counter; getState().fps gives current (last 1s), average and min (last 10s), sampleSeconds and source (window/xr). min is null until a full second is measured. Absent without fps=1.
?cues=<base64url UTF-8 JSON array of {"line":"..."}> : start an injected script.

API:
window.puppetStage.getState()
  {step, mouth, tracked, stage, gloveProgress, index, count, line, cueLine}
  step: raise-hand | glove-on | open-hand | next-line | script | improv
  mouth: measured/smoothed 0..1; index: zero-based script index (-1 for empty).
  line: full logical guide/cue text (retains the legacy "Line N:" prefix); cueLine: underlying script line.
  The sign strips that prefix and shows N/count separately; line is not a paginated fragment.
window.puppetStage.loadCues([{line:"A button asks for a speaking part."}])
  Starts script mode at index 0. Accepts 0..100 plain-text lines, 1..160 characters.
  Invalid input throws TypeError without changing state. [] clears the board.
window.puppetStage.nextCue()
  Same progression as right-hand pinch/swipe. Ignored before next-line step.
  After the last script line: optional friend, duet, improv, then Make a take.
window.puppetStage.setStage("placeholder")
  Preserves guide, hand and script. Unknown names throw RangeError unchanged.
The original cue/stage calls return fresh state snapshots. No mouth setter is exposed.

Hands-only example after clicking Enter VR:
const r = window.__iwer.remote;
await r.dispatch('run_sequence', {device:'hand-right', idleHand:'keep', body:'fixed', gaze:'fixed', steps:[{anchor:'wrist', position:{x:0.08,y:1.02,z:-0.43}, orientation:{fingers:'forward',palm:'down'}, poseId:'fist', duration:0.45}]});
await r.dispatch('set_hand_pose', {device:'hand-right',poseId:'open',duration:0.25});
// Wait until getState().step is next-line, then:
await r.dispatch('select', {device:'hand-right',duration:0.2});
await r.dispatch('run_sequence', {device:'hand-right',idleHand:'keep',body:'fixed',gaze:'fixed',steps:[{microgesture:'swipe-left'}]});
// Wait at least 450ms between separate advances. No controllers are used.
// window.__iwer is available only with emu=1. The panel uses the same commands.

Evidence: app/harness/run.mjs -> app/harness-out/summary.json, screenshots, run.webm.
Diagnostic window.__puppetLog timestamps are milliseconds from page navigation.

Take recording / playback (v1, local page memory only):
After script -> friend invitation (raise left to accept, right pinch/swipe to skip)
-> four-line Teal/Amber duet -> improv -> pinch -> Make a take -> pinch starts.
During recording right pinch/swipe advances/wraps the script. Both RAISED hands
held in fists for 2 seconds stop and automatically replay. Lower hands during
replay: puppets keep acting. At take-ready, swipe replays; pinch starts a new take.
At most 3 takes are kept, newest first. Each is capped at 180s (auto-finish).

window.puppetStage.exportTake(index=0)
  Returns a fresh JSON-compatible Take object or null. JSON.stringify to serialize.
window.puppetStage.loadTake(json)
  Accepts a JSON string or object; validates before any mutation, returns
  {frames,duration,count}. Throws for invalid data or while recording.
window.puppetStage.playTake(index=0)
  Starts playback at frame 0, returns {mode:'playing'}. Throws for no such take
  or while recording. Also works without entering VR.
window.puppetStage.listTakes()
  [{index,duration,frames}], newest first; max length 3.
window.puppetStage.getPlaybackTrace()
  [{t,right,left}] at each applied 1/60s tick, measured from the rendered jaws.
?take=<base64url UTF-8 JSON Take>
  Load and automatically play. Invalid input is ignored/logged. Use loadTake for
  long records (URL length limits vary). Nothing is uploaded or persisted.

Take = {version:1, step:1/60, duration:N/60, frames:Frame[], events:Event[]}
Frame = {t:i/60, right:Hand, left:Hand, line:string, index:number, count:number,
         speaker:string, stage:'a'|'placeholder', scene:number}
Hand = {tracked:boolean, visible:boolean, mouth:0..1, rest:0..1,
        position:[x,y,z], rotation:[x,y,z,w], joints:{[XRJointName]:Pose}}
Pose = {position:[x,y,z], rotation:[x,y,z,w]}
All 25 valid WebXR joint poses on each side are captured; unavailable joints are
absent. Positions are reference-space metres, +Y up/-Z forward; rotations are
unit quaternions. Hand's outer pose is the anchored, smoothed puppet root in seated stage space. Times are seconds
from take start; index and scene are zero-based. scene drives stage.transition.
Event = {t,type:'cue',index,line} | {t,type:'scene',index,stage}
Events are derived again from validated frames on import. Lines are plain text.
Maximum 10800 frames, 64 MiB JSON string, supported stage only, finite values.
Live sampling uses sample-and-hold of XR poses with 60 Hz smoothing. Playback
bypasses live input and applies recorded joints/root/mouth/cue/scene snapshots
at 1/60s. Hidden tabs pause; stalls over 1s pause the excess. No random mouth.

getState additionally returns leftMouth, leftTracked, friend, speaker, takeMode
(live|recording|playing|review), takeCount, recordingSeconds, playbackFrame,
stopHoldSeconds, audio:{muted,volume,state,syllables:[rightCount,leftCount]}.
Additional steps: friend | duet | make-take | recording | playback | take-ready.
Take methods return the values documented above, not general state snapshots.

Voice prototype (voice.ts): original additive Web Audio babble, no sound assets
or speech service. A mouth crossing 0.3 produces one syllable; below 0.18 rearms.
Opening controls pitch/amplitude. Teal=170 Hz base, Amber=245 Hz base.
Enabled by default after user activation; ?mute=1 disables it. Left thumb forward
raises volume by .1, backward lowers by .1 (0..1, initial .55). Hand gamepad
buttons 7/8 or wrist-local thumb-travel fallback when absent. Controller input
has no effect. Amber knit is #F2A541; same cream #F5E9D3 buttons as Teal.

Evidence additionally includes take-example.json and replay-traces.json.
summary.json includes each stage's pageMilliseconds, two-replay maxDifference,
recording-to-applied-jaw maxAppliedError, and a nested-path dist loading check.
No new npm dependencies; existing MIT packages and native Web APIs only.

Tabletop scenery:
Cue may also include scene: "night-town" | "seaside" | "moon" (default night-town).
getState().scene returns the visible scenery name, including night-town during the initial guide and the dominant visible panel during a slide. Frame.scene stores its numeric
index (0/1/2); scene changes are independent of the gesture used to advance.
The sign first fits one row using 80–100% font size. Longer lines use two balanced pages at punctuation or word boundaries, with the current N/count in the corner.
The stage provides puppet anchors, movement bounds, scale and neutral facing.
New XR sessions wait for the first valid viewer pose, then align the stage to its position/yaw. A reference-space reset waits for the next valid pose, realigns the stage and reacquires both hand neutrals. Pitch does not tilt the tabletop. The eye-level stage anchor is 0.60m forward.
?emu=1 narrows the display field of view; real headset optics are untouched.
?mute=1 disables both babble and synthesized audience applause.

Optional compact JSON (v2, native Web Compression API, no information loss):
await window.puppetStage.exportCompactTake(index=0)
  => {version:2, encoding:"gzip-base64", data:string} or null.
await window.puppetStage.loadCompactTake(json)
  Validates decompressed v1 data, preserving every joint and mouth value.
  Returns {frames,duration,count}; call playTake() to replay.
exportTake/loadTake retain their synchronous v1 format for compatibility.
The decompressed size is limited to 64 MiB; no data leaves the page.

Sharing a show (v3, URL fragment only):
await window.puppetStage.exportShareLink(index=0)
  => absolute URL with #t=3.<base64url-gzip>. Rejects missing takes, takes over
  30 seconds or payloads over 64 KiB. Removes all query parameters (including
  emu, capture, cues and legacy take). Does not upload, navigate or copy by itself.
After a hands-only recording stops, the XR sign says
"Saved. Exit VR to share this take." The 2D "Share this take" button copies the
link after leaving VR; copying is optional. Clipboard-denied browsers show a
selectable link. No share button or controller action is added inside VR.

Opening #t= shows "A show for you" and the 2D "Watch the show" button. It plays
in the normal browser canvas after that click, with the existing synthesized
babble (not recorded voice). Enter VR also starts/resumes the show, then returns
to "Raise your right hand to answer" and the ordinary hand introduction.
getState().sharePhase is none | ready | playing | ended.
Malformed, truncated, unsupported-version and oversized fragments fall back
silently to the ordinary page. No fragment is sent in an HTTP request.

The v3 allowlist contains only stage-local root position (1mm), quaternion
smallest-three components (signed 16-bit plus omitted component index), mouth
and puppet droop (8-bit), visibility, dialogue/scene/speaker transitions and
an optional injected script. No joints, viewer/camera pose, microphone audio,
wall-clock timestamps, identifiers or query parameters are included.
30 Hz base samples use integer deltas, zigzag varints, native CompressionStream
(gzip) and URL-safe base64. Sparse quantized midpoint curve corrections preserve
sharp hand changes that linear 30 Hz interpolation cannot reproduce within the
error budget. Discrete cue/visibility transitions retain their original 60 Hz
frame index; playback reconstructs the existing 60 Hz timeline. Maximum 1800
playback frames, 64 KiB token and 512 KiB decompressed data, validated atomically.
Custom cue text is included as text, just as shown on the sign.

getPlaybackTrace additionally records applied stage-local rightPosition /
leftPosition, rightRotation / leftRotation, line, speaker and scene for numeric
replay comparisons. No camera pose is added to the trace or the shared format.
Verification: npm run test:shares; SHARE=1 node harness/share-run.mjs.
Sharing capture: node harness/share-capture.mjs (see harness/SHARING.md).
